exposure: risk factors for PROM (previous PPROM, idiopathic causes)
outcome: maternal morbidity (puerperal pyrexia, wound gape, maternal mortality)
neonatal outcomes (NICU admission, gestational age at delivery)
cohort: 120 patients with a history of prelabour rupture of membranes (PROM) before the onset of labor were included.
finding: PROM is a significant obstetric issue with identified risk factors, leading to maternal and neonatal morbidities, and conservative management may increase gestational age at delivery and likelihood of vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Vaginal vertex delivery was the most common mode (60%), and conservative management strategies for PROM may lead to an increased likelihood of vaginal birth.
gest_age: Most PROM cases occurred between 28-31+6 weeks of gestation (48.3%), with 46.6% of neonates born at term.
